items.title: Patient-Centered Observations of Outpatient Hemodialysis: An Exploratory Systems Approach to Understanding Infection Prevention Using Human Factors.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Infection remains the second leading cause of death in patients with ESKD on hemodialysis. This exploratory analysis sought to characterize interruptions and non-routine events (NREs), in the outpatient dialysis setting, with particular interest in the relationships between interruptions and NREs and infection prevention and control (IPC) activities. METHODS: We conducted a mixed-methods, observational, exploratory study of 45 patients and their dialysis teams across four U.S. dialysis facilities (99 total outpatient hemodialysis treatments hours observed). Structured observations were focused on the team surrounding an individual patient for the duration of their dialysis session using a modified Line Operations Safety Audit (LOSA) approach. Quantitative analyses were conducted. RESULTS: A technician simultaneously caring for four patients can experience a median of 64 interruptions, or 16 per patient (range 3-50) during their treatment time. The phases with greatest risk of infection (i.e., connection, disconnection) had a significantly higher time required to complete (with NRE: connection 14:37, disconnection 13:41; without NRE: connection 7:32, disconnection 8:18). Thirty-seven of 45 patients experienced at least one NRE during clinical care, defined as a patient-related clinical event (e.g., long clotting time) or an operational variation (e.g., transportation problem). Findings are exploratory in nature and provide support for future hypothesis generation and testing. CONCLUSIONS: Interruptions and NREs were frequent in the outpatient dialysis work system, and connection and disconnection times were longer when an NRE was present. Since these disruptions occurred during phases that include IPC-related activities, they may introduce competing demands that could challenge consistent adherence, though adherence was not directly measured. These exploratory findings may inform the design of workflows and processes that better support IPC and patient safety in the outpatient dialysis setting.

items.title: PENGARUH PENGGUNAAN AI GENERATIF TERHADAP KEMANDIRIAN BELAJAR MAHASISWA GENERASI Z
items.abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of Generative AI usage on the learning independence of Generation Z students at STIT Darul Ulum Kotabaru, viewed from the perspective of perceived ease of use and potential dependency. The research employs a quantitative approach with an associative causal design. Data were collected through questionnaires distributed to Generation Z students who have used Generative AI in academic activities. The variables examined include perceived ease of use of Generative AI (X1), potential dependency on Generative AI (X2), and student learning independence (Y). Data analysis was conducted using multiple linear regression with SPSS. The results indicate that perceived ease of use and potential dependency simultaneously influence students' learning independence. Generative AI provides significant convenience in accessing information, understanding materials, and completing academic tasks. However, excessive use without critical thinking and academic responsibility can lead to dependency that reduces learning independence. This study contributes to the development of educational technology studies, particularly in understanding the impact of Generative AI on student learning behavior in Islamic higher education institutions

items.title: Perbandingan Decision Tree dan Random Forest untuk Deteksi Dini Diabetes
items.abstract: Diabetes mellitus merupakan gangguan metabolik kronis yang membutuhkan deteksi dini agar komplikasi jangka panjang dapat dicegah sejak awal. Penelitian ini membandingkan kinerja prediktif dua algoritma klasifikasi berbasis pohon, yaitu Decision Tree dan Random Forest, dalam mendeteksi diabetes pada tahap awal menggunakan dataset Pima Indians Diabetes dari UCI Machine Learning Repository. Sebagai pelengkap, penelitian ini juga menerapkan kerangka Explainable Artificial Intelligence lima lapis yang memanfaatkan SHAP guna menghasilkan penjelasan model yang relevan secara klinis, mulai dari kepentingan fitur global hingga validasi terhadap pengetahuan patofisiologi. Rekayasa fitur dilakukan untuk memperluas ruang fitur dari 8 menjadi 14 variabel, sementara tahap praproses meliputi stratified train-test split, imputasi median, winsorizing berbasis IQR, normalisasi Min-Max, dan SMOTE untuk menyeimbangkan distribusi kelas yang tidak proporsional. Optimasi hyperparameter dilakukan melalui GridSearchCV dengan Stratified K-Fold sebanyak lima lipatan, menggunakan F1-Score sebagai kriteria utama. Hasil eksperimen menunjukkan bahwa Random Forest secara konsisten mengungguli Decision Tree pada seluruh metrik evaluasi, dengan F1-Score cross-validation sebesar 0,9002 berbanding 0,8687 dan ROC-AUC pada set pengujian sebesar 80,61% berbanding 70,43%. McNemar Test menunjukkan bahwa perbedaan pola kesalahan klasifikasi antar kedua model tidak signifikan secara statistik pada ukuran sampel yang tersedia, namun pertimbangan multidimensional seperti stabilitas cross-validation dan selisih ROC-AUC tetap mendukung rekomendasi terhadap Random Forest. Analisis SHAP mengonfirmasi bahwa Insulin, Glucose, dan rasio Insulin terhadap Glucose merupakan tiga prediktor paling berpengaruh, sejalan dengan mekanisme patofisiologi diabetes tipe 2 yang telah mapan dalam literatur kedokteran. Penelitian ini juga mengakui keterbatasan generalisabilitas dataset terhadap populasi Indonesia sebagai catatan penting bagi penelitian lanjutan.

items.title: Percepciones sobre IA en la educación superior salteña
items.abstract: In this article, I aim to analyze the perceptions and uses of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) among students at Higher Education Institutes (HEIs) in Salta. Through a mixed-methods approach based on surveys, it investigates the tension between the massive student adoption for autonomous learning and the infrastructural shortcomings that deepen the digital divide in a local context. The obtained sample evidences a predominant enthusiasm for the emancipatory potential of GenAI, although ethical concerns persist regarding data reliability and the fear of replacing the teaching role. It is observed that the appropriation of AI occurs mostly in a delocalized manner and without pedagogical support, highlighting the urgency to update teacher training while also promoting public policies that guarantee a critical and inclusive integration.

items.title: Perceptions of ChatGPT- and veterinarian-generated responses to pet owners’ medical questions
items.abstract: Background Artificial Intelligence (AI) is becoming increasingly significant in veterinary medicine, particularly in answering pet owners’ medical questions. AI’s integration could reduce veterinary professionals’ workload while improving access to medical advice. However, the reliability and quality of AI-generated responses compared to veterinarians’ remain unexplored. The objective was to determine whether AI-generated responses were perceived as comparable to veterinarian-generated responses. Methods This cross-sectional study analysed the answers to a sample of pet owners’ medical questions. Both a veterinarian and ChatGPT (GPT-4o, May 2024) provided answers, which were anonymised and presented in a survey distributed through mailing lists and public Facebook groups. Participants were asked to assess each response based on structure, quality, and empathy, using a five-point Likert scale. They then had to indicate whether they trusted the response, and which response they preferred. Results Over two-thirds of the 201 participants (68%) preferred the ChatGPT-generated answers ( p < 0.05), which were rated higher in structure, quality, and empathy. Limitations This study has several limitations, including a small sample size, reliance on a single veterinarian, and use of only two Reddit-derived scenarios. Response accuracy was not assessed, and word count restrictions may have affected perceived response quality. Additionally, prior research suggests that irrelevant patient details can impact ChatGPT’s accuracy, raising questions about user trust if clinical inaccuracies were present. Conclusion AI-generated responses received higher participant ratings in structure, quality and empathy, suggesting AI may enhance veterinary client communication when used under appropriate professional supervision.

items.title: Perspectives on inverse design for AI magnonics
items.abstract: Abstract Inverse design - specifying a desired functionality and letting a computational algorithm search for a structure that meets it - has emerged as a powerful paradigm for magnonic device engineering. In this article, we survey the rapidly growing field of inverse-design magnonics, organising it along two axes: the design variables (topology, material parameters, and magnetic field landscape) and the algorithmic toolbox (gradient-free, gradient-based, and neural-network-based methods) together with the differentiable micromagnetic solvers that enable them. We then identify open frontiers that we consider most promising for the next phase of the field: sensitivity analysis and robust design to bridge the gap between simulation and experiment; input shaping and transducer optimisation; the incorporation of nonlinear spin-wave effects as an explicit design resource; spatially structured amplification; self-adapting media and machine-learning-based design; and the long-term vision of a universal, reconfigurable magnonic platform. We argue that magnonics and artificial intelligence are converging from two directions-machine-learning tools for designing magnonic devices, and magnonic devices as hardware for neuromorphic computation-and propose the term AI magnonics to describe this emerging paradigm.

items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, is fundamentally transforming academic work in higher education, reshaping teaching, research, data analysis, scholarly writing, and the resolution of increasingly complex academic tasks. Nevertheless, access to and use of AI does not automatically translate into effective AI-enabled academic capability. The gap between merely “using AI” and developing meaningful human–AI collaboration has therefore emerged as a critical issue in contemporary faculty development. This study aims to identify and empirically examine the factors shaping lecturers’ competence in effectively leveraging AI to address complex academic tasks in non-public universities in Vietnam. Particular attention is given to the roles of AI literacy, AI self-efficacy, Human–AI Collaboration Competence, and critical AI use, while examining institutional AI support as a potential moderating mechanism. A sequential mixed-methods design is proposed. The qualitative phase employs expert interviews and/or a Delphi process to develop, refine, and validate the conceptual dimensions and measurement indicators. The quantitative phase involves a large-scale survey of lecturers working in Vietnamese non-public universities. Structural equation modelling, using PLS-SEM or CB-SEM depending on data characteristics and model specifications, is employed to examine direct, mediating, and moderating relationships among the proposed constructs. The study is designed to identify the mechanisms through which AI literacy and AI self-efficacy are transformed into Human–AI Collaboration Competence, Critical AI Use, and AI-Enabled Academic Task Competence, ultimately contributing to lecturers’ capacity to perform complex academic tasks effectively. The proposed model provides an integrated explanation of how individual capabilities and institutional conditions jointly shape AI-enabled academic performance. The study proposes an AI-Enabled Academic Capability Development Model as a conceptual and empirical foundation for faculty development in the global digital era. The findings are expected to provide practical implications for non-public universities in designing AI competency development programmes, strengthening institutional AI support ecosystems, and promoting critical, responsible, and academically productive human–AI collaboration.

items.title: Physiological activation regimes reveal distinct autonomic mechanisms underlying operational performance under cognitive workload and stress
items.abstract: Human performance in safety-critical environments depends on the interaction between mental workload, stress, autonomic regulation, and behavior. This study investigated whether associations between heart rate variability (HRV) and performance varied across physiological activation ranges and operational contexts during a multi-task flight simulation implemented through the AeroStim platform. Forty-two healthy participants (25 ± 5 years) performed either a Workload-Only condition (WO; n = 20), comprising Tracking and System Monitoring tasks, or a Stress-Oriented condition (SO; n = 22), in which additional stress-inducing tasks were concurrently administered. ECG was continuously recorded using an EqVital wearable T-shirt. Linear and non-linear HRV indices were extracted and normalized within participants using Min-Max scaling. Gaussian Mixture Modeling of normalized SDNN identified three relative, subject-specific activation ranges ( Easy, Medium , and Hard ), with classification showing high stability across alternative normalization procedures. HRV-performance associations were assessed using Spearman correlations with permutation-based inference and Benjamini–Hochberg correction, while performance differences were evaluated using non-parametric tests. HRV-performance correlations varied across activation ranges and contexts; none passed FDR correction, so these should be considered exploratory. In WO, associations involved LF in the Easy range, SDNN, SD2, and LF in the Medium range, and SDNN, LF/HF, and Sample Entropy in the Hard range. In SO, associations in the Medium range extended to vagal, global variability, and non-linear complexity indices, while Hard-range associations mainly involved vagal and LF-related measures. Omission rate was lower at Medium than Easy activation in WO, providing partial support for an intermediate activation advantage, whereas no consistent performance optimum emerged across contexts. Between-condition comparisons revealed a robust speed-accuracy trade-off, with WO producing faster but less accurate responses and SO producing slower but more accurate responses. Sensitivity analysis further indicated that differences in exercise windows affected HRV metrics in a metric-dependent manner, with greater deviations generally observed for frequency-domain measures. The findings suggest that HRV-performance relationships are context- and activation-dependent rather than captured by a single universal marker. The results support the potential of regime-based, multimodal HRV monitoring for adaptive human-machine systems, while highlighting the need for standardized recording durations, independent autonomic markers, and validation across individuals and real operational environments.

items.title: Precision Pharmacotherapy in Vitiligo
items.abstract: Precision pharmacotherapy is a paradigm shift in managing vitiligo that has shifted from a one size fits all approach to a stratified, mechanism based approach. This chapter introduces an integrated approach addressing clinical phenotype, immune endotype, and therapeutic mechanism to maximize the use of both topical and systemic, as well as targeted Janus kinase inhibitors. Potency-stratified topicals, pulse systemic immunomodulators and selective JAK1 or JAK1/JAK2 or JAK3/TEC inhibitors fit into a step-up algorithm based on disease activity, anatomical location, age and comorbidity. The discussion highlights emerging enablers like lesion mapping using artificial intelligence, digital phenotyping, digital twins, and pharmacogenomic prediction as tools for response prediction on extent scoring and decision support for durable, personalized repigmentation with balanced safety.

items.title: Predicting Faults in Mechanical Systems Using Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
items.abstract: The occurrence of unexpected malfunctions of mechanical systems such as bearings, gearboxes, turbofan engines, and other rotating machinery is still the main cause of downtime, safety hazards, and maintenance cost throughout the manufacturing, energy, and transportation sectors. Recent technological advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) technology have transformed fault prediction from an entirely physics-based activity to a data-based activity, in which sensors, signal processing, and learning algorithms estimate the health state of a machine together. This paper provides a structured assessment and comparative synthesis of AI/ML fault-prediction literature. Nineteen peer-reviewed studies obtained from scholarly and web-based databases for the period 2011–2026 are reviewed. A review of the two main tasks: fault diagnosis – classification of fault type, location and severity – prognosis – prediction of remaining useful life, RUL. The evidence is structured into a six-stage pipeline – data acquisition, pre-processing, feature extraction, model training, output, maintenance decision. The analysis is conducted using various test rigs including the CWRU bearings as well as NASA C-MAPSS turbofan engines and gearbox. The results show that on these benchmarks, convolutional and recurrent deep architectures, attention-augmented LSTMs, and ensemble methods consistently outperform classical classifiers; root-mean-square errors (RMSE) on C-MAPSS RUL errors are about 12 cycles and classification accuracies on CWRU exceed 98%. Simultaneously, the review also outlines a number of ongoing open challenges, like data scarcity, domain shift, class imbalance, limited interpretability, and overoptimistic evaluation, which must be overcome before lab results can become consistent with the reliable deployment in the industry. items.title: Preserving traditional plant knowledge via AI-driven identification and human-centered mobile design
items.abstract: The loss of indigenous botanical knowledge poses risks to biodiversity conservation and community health by weakening the knowledge of medicinal plants and their traditional use as local plant-based health care options. An integrated system that combines deep learning image recognition with a user-friendly mobile interface to document and preserve medicinal plant knowledge is presented in this study. A Convolutional neural network (CNN) was trained on a curated dataset of fourteen Nigerian medicinal plants, achieving 78.9% validation accuracy in species identification. Recognized plants are linked to an expert-curated knowledge base (with features, compounds, and uses) structured as a graph for efficient retrieval. A mobile app prototype was also designed with intuitive user interfaces, such as a landing page for navigation and an image-based search screen for plant identification. The Human-Computer Interaction (HCI)-driven design emphasizes ease-of-use, with clear labels and minimal steps, enabling users (including elders and youth) to capture plant images and instantly access scientific and local names, medicinal properties, and usage guidelines. In “active learning” mode, low-confidence predictions trigger the retrieval of similar examples to guide users. This Artificial Intelligence plus Human-Computer Interaction approach addresses issues of manual identification (subjectivity, expertise gap) by automating recognition and by empowering communities to digitally record ethnobotanical knowledge. By improving accessibility to reliable plant data, this system contributes to Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) 3 and 15.

items.title: Priority-Weighted System Dynamics for Cost-Effective Risk Mitigation in High-Risk Storage Facilities
items.abstract: High-risk storage facilities function as sociotechnical systems in which technical reliability, human performance, organizational control, and environmental stress interact over time, so their risk cannot be captured by a single probability-impact score. This study develops a priority-weighted System Dynamics model to evaluate risk mitigation strategies prior to implementation, using ammunition storage as the empirical case. Analytic Network Process (ANP) weights, validated through a Fuzzy Delphi panel, are embedded directly in the stock-flow structure so that the relative importance of interdependent risk factors shapes how risk evolves under each policy. Over a 60-month horizon, the baseline raised the Total Risk Index (TRI) from 29.65 to 44.57, whereas full implementation of the prioritized mitigation set lowered it to 14.88. Under a 50% budget, ANP-guided allocation reduced the index to 24.04, while equal allocation under the same budget raised it to 38.77. The prioritized limited-budget scenario also achieved the highest Cost-Effectiveness Ratio (CER) (2.518). The model supports comparative scenario evaluation and engineering decision-making rather than deterministic prediction of explosion events.

items.title: Process-oriented approach to anti-crisis management of an enterprise
items.abstract: In the modern conditions of the market economy, the organization is characterized by a functional approach to enterprise management. However, the frequent occurrence of crisis phenomena has shown that this approach is too cumbersome and does not allow for timely response to negative conditions. A more flexible approach is needed to manage the organization more effectively. Thus, the process approach is more appropriate, with its help it is possible to develop and optimize various business processes and optimize the whole process in general. The use of a process approach minimizes the impact of the human factor, reduces costs, increases flexibility and speed of management decision-making, and allows for timely response to changes in the external and internal environment. This approach is relevant and serves as an effective solution and prevention method for crisis situations.

items.title: Prompt-as-a-Protocol with Agentic Research Automation: A Validated Methodology for AI-Native Biomedical Data Science Producing Peer-Reviewed Findings Across Genomics and Biosensor Domains
items.abstract: Recent advances in large language model (LLM)-driven agentic systems have demonstrated capabilities for automating biomedical data analysis workflows. However, existing systems are predominantly validated on synthetic benchmarks or retrospective tasks, without demonstrated production of novel, peer-reviewed biological findings. Here we describe Prompt-as-a-Protocol (PaaP), a methodology that converts natural-language research questions into structured, executable analytical protocols, coupled with an agentic Generative Research Automation (GRA) layer that executes these protocols with integrated quality assurance. We validate PaaP+GRA through two prospective case studies in distinct biomedical domains. In single-cell transcriptomics, the pipeline identified KIF3A as the sole genome-wide significant correlate of ciliation status in human striatal parvalbumin interneurons (adjusted p = 1.37 x 10-14), while autonomously detecting and correcting a sex composition confound (p = 8.1 x 10-44) that would have produced spurious results. In biosensor analytics, the pipeline achieved calibrated PPG-to-ECG heart rate variability classification matching gold-standard ECG performance (ROC AUC = 0.85) for stress-state discrimination relevant to alcohol use disorder relapse monitoring. Both studies have been submitted for peer review. To our knowledge, PaaP+GRA is the first prompt-to-protocol methodology validated by prospective production of novel biological findings across multiple domains, including autonomous confound detection, rather than benchmark performance alone.

items.title: Protecting Trademark in the Metaverse: The Emerging Threat of AI-Generated Counterfeits
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence tools allow metaverse users to generate virtual wearables, avatar accessories and other branded goods, which often infringe upon trademark rights. These infringing goods, however, are not static counterfeits but dynamically generated knockoffs that rarely explicitly name the trademark owner and take place in novel digital environments. This paper analyses whether and how Indian trademark laws can tackle such emerging forms of infringement based on the doctrine of “use in the course of trade”, the “identical or similar goods” jurisdictional anchor and the “likelihood of confusion” standard. It argues that the ability of Indian trademark law to address these concerns is limited by the very existence of doctrines and tests that seek to make sense of trademark infringement in virtual settings, as well as the lack of a holistic regulatory approach to the liability of metaverse platforms under the Trade Marks Act, 1999 and the Information Technology Act, 2000. By relying on recent Indian, EU, US and UK jurisprudence and early cases on trademarks and AI-generated counterfeits, the paper highlights the jurisdictional fragmentation in addressing generative AI infringement in India and proposes a unified approach to enforcing trademark rights against dynamically generated virtual counterfeits.

items.title: Psychological Outcomes and Correlates Associated with Over-Reliance on Artificial Intelligence Tools: An Integrative Review
items.abstract: Abstract The growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) has raised concerns about over-reliance and its psychological implications. This integrative review synthesised psychological outcomes and correlates associated with AI over-reliance and examined its conceptualisation and measurement. The review included 28 studies identified through database and citation searching. AI over-reliance was associated with depression, anxiety, psychological distress, and cognitive disengagement, while findings concerning well-being and self-related functioning, including self-efficacy and autonomy, were mixed and context-dependent. Evidence concerning social or relational functioning was particularly limited, with only one included study directly examining this domain as an outcome. Most evidence was cross-sectional and therefore did not establish temporal direction or causality. Notably, the only longitudinal study found that depression and anxiety predicted subsequent AI dependence, whereas dependence did not predict later depression or anxiety, suggesting that psychological distress may precede dependence. No consensus definition or measure emerged; studies examined reliance, psychological dependence, problematic or compulsive use, and addiction-like engagement. AI over-reliance is therefore best understood as an overarching, multidimensional concept. These findings highlight the need for clearer conceptual boundaries, standardised measurement, and longitudinal and experimental research. PROSPERO CRD420251038303.

items.title: Public-Sector AI Adoption Toolkit
items.abstract: A practical, vendor-neutral toolkit for public institutions that want employees to use generative AI tools in everyday written work while protecting institutional information and keeping a person accountable for every official product. It is designed for document-intensive teams such as internal control, internal audit, oversight, legal support, procurement, and program administration. The toolkit has five parts that can be used separately or together: Risk Classification Worksheet: four classes of AI use, from low risk to prohibited, with a step-by-step classification guide and a use register. Human-Review Protocol: de-identification and redaction before AI use, structured instructions with the PACTO method, a technical review checklist, validation and signature, and specialized assistants for repetitive processes. Role-Based Curriculum Outline: a twelve-hour course in three sessions with step-by-step hands-on practice. Pilot Measurement Template: baselines defined in advance and reports that keep observations separate from causal conclusions. Facilitator Guide: preparing internal staff to deliver later cohorts. The toolkit systematizes practices the author developed in Brazilian public administration from 2024 to 2026, described in Gomes (2026), arXiv:2606.01517.

items.title: Quantum Haar Wavelet Transform methods applications and hardware realizations in quantum computing
items.abstract: Abstract Quantum Haar Wavelet Transform (QHWT) methods connect multiresolution analysis with quantum information processing through reversible averaging and differencing operations that can be implemented with comparatively compact circuits. Their localized basis functions, real-valued binary structure, and compatibility with hierarchical state representations make them attractive for resource-constrained quantum processing. Nevertheless, claims of practical superiority are difficult to generalize because published studies use heterogeneous encodings, simulators, hardware platforms, noise models, and evaluation metrics. This systematic review examines scholarly work on Haar-based quantum methods published between 1997 and March 2025. A PRISMA-oriented protocol was used to search major engineering and computing databases, remove duplicates, screen records, assess eligibility, and construct a qualitative evidence corpus. The review includes peer-reviewed journal and conference studies together with a limited number of historically influential technical reports and preprints; therefore, the corpus is described as scholarly literature rather than as a uniformly peer-reviewed dataset. Because the reported experiments are not sufficiently homogeneous for statistical pooling, numerical results are treated as study-specific evidence rather than global averages. The review makes three analytical contributions. First, it introduces a unified conceptual framework that links mathematical foundations, circuit realization, application design, hardware evaluation, and research translation. Second, it develops a taxonomy spanning transform theory, quantum image and signal processing, hardware implementation, and emerging quantum artificial intelligence and security applications. Third, it critically compares QHWT with Quantum Fourier Transform and higher-order wavelet approaches by distinguishing circuit depth, gate complexity, approximation behavior, hardware assumptions, and empirical validation. The synthesis indicates that QHWT is most compelling when localization, reversible multiresolution processing, and shallow circuit structure are more important than smooth-basis approximation. Individual studies report promising compression, feature-extraction, and hardware-efficiency results, but these findings remain conditional on encoding choices and platform constraints. Important limitations include sparse cross-platform benchmarking, limited fault-tolerant analysis, noise sensitivity, uncertain scaling, and optimization difficulties in variational quantum learning, including barren plateaus. The resulting roadmap prioritizes reproducible benchmarks, hardware-aware circuit design, explicit complexity reporting, error-mitigation studies, and validation on larger quantum systems.

items.title: Queuing Theory as the Interpretable Core of Adaptive Hospital Operations: A Theory-Building Synthesis and the LASI Framework
items.abstract: Hospital patient flow and resource allocation are problems of decision-making under stochastic, non-stationary demand in a complex adaptive system, yet analytical queuing models, simulation, and artificial intelligence (AI) are treated as competing techniques, and no theory specifies how an interpretable core could safely constrain an adaptive one. This paper makes a theory-building contribution. It formalizes hospital operations as a single controlled-stochastic-process problem — defending that abstraction against network-optimization, partially-observable, cyber-physical, and decentralized alternatives — of which the analytical, simulation, and learning paradigms are three approximation strategies. From four functional requirements it derives the LASI framework (Layered Analytical–Simulation–Intelligence), argues each layer’s indispensability and the necessity of their dependency ordering, and specifies the core mechanism as a constrained-Markov-decision-process safety filter. Its most developed contribution is the validity-region mechanism: the analytical core may bound learning only where the core is validated, with the boundary estimated continuously by simulation through an analytical–reality divergence measure, and authority transferring between the analytical and simulation layers by a hysteresis rule. Governance is elevated from a passive gate to an active supervisory controller that resolves inter-layer conflicts and sets a responsible decision weight — the delegable authority to learning that keeps violation risk below a governance tolerance. Seven falsifiable propositions with boundary conditions state the theory. The synthesis repositions queuing theory not as a stage superseded by AI but as the interpretable, auditable core of accountable adaptive hospital operations.

items.abstract: A reality-constrained multi-agent framework modeling system survival under joint constraints of energy, trust, and entropy. We show that system stability undergoes sharp threshold transitions governed by a coupled entropy-trust-energy collapse mechanism. items.title: Recent advances and challenges in electronic nose technology for agricultural commodities and food quality assessment
items.abstract: Traditional methods for analyzing agricultural produce and food quality, such as chromatography and sensory evaluation, are often expensive, time consuming, and require skilled professionals, making them hard to implement for rapid and large-scale testing. The advent of Electronic nose (E-Nose) technology presents a promising alternative by emulating the human olfactory system through sensor arrays that identify volatile compounds and produce distinctive response patterns. This review examines the principles, evolution, and applications of E-nose systems for assessing the quality of food and agricultural products across diverse categories, including fish, meat, dairy products, tea, coffee, and edible oils. These systems provide non-destructive and smart analytical solutions for modern food-processing industries. Their role in identifying contamination, freshness assessment, authenticity, and monitoring fermentation plays a crucial role in modern food processing. Recent advancements integrating artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methodologies have significantly enhanced the efficacy of E-nose systems, enabling superior pattern recognition, data interpretation, and precise prediction capabilities. This enables objective and accurate quality assessment. Despite these advantages, the widespread adoption of this technology is hindered due to sensor drift, low sensitivity, high initial costs, and the difficulty of processing such complex data. Future research should focus on enhancing sensor stability, formulating resilient data analytics models, and decreasing system costs to facilitate scalability. Overall, E-nose technology has potential to transform food-quality assessment by providing the food industry with rapid, non-destructive, and intelligent analytical methods.

items.title: Reducing Domain-Specific Hallucinations in LLMs via Expert Context Injection without Model Retraining: A Governed Inference Framework and Controlled Ablation Study
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) frequently produce plausible yet incorrect outputs when tasked with specialized domains such as legal document analysis or software engineering. While fine-tuning and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) are common remedies, they introduce significant computational overhead, architectural complexity, or privacy risks when proprietary knowledge is involved. We introduce a Governed Inference Framework that reduces domain-specific errors by injecting expert-governed context at inference time without modifying model weights. The framework orchestrates task characterization, expert selection, bounded response generation, and independent verification. We report a controlled ablation study across five experimental conditions (A–E) and five paired repetitions (350 total outputs) on a frozen synthetic bank of 14 specialized cases. A 26B-parameter model operating within the full framework (Condition E) achieved 71.4% exact responses (50/70) and mean F1 = 0.932, compared to 0% exact (0/70, F1 = 0.179) for a professional prompt (Condition A), 21.4% exact (15/70, F1 ≈ 0.50) for static expert context (Condition B), and 8.6% exact (6/70, F1 = 0.436) for orchestration without verification (Condition D). Critically, Conditions B and C received identical context bytes (SHA-256 verified), yet Condition C (NeuroSkill runtime) preserved operational capabilities validation, modular selection, versioning, budget control, and verifiable receipts that Condition B lacked. A paired sign-test confirmed that the full framework outperformed the prompt baseline in all 14 cases (p = 0.000122) and outperformed orchestration without verification in 13 of 14 cases (p = 0.000244). We complement the semantic study with an independent operational confirmatory suite (56/56 tests passed) demonstrating that the full system enforces fail-closed behavior: an independent evaluator detects incorrect outputs, and a publication gate raises a Document Quality Error before any non-exact result reaches the user or codebase. The operational matrix assigns 85/100 to the NeuroSkill runtime, 95/100 to the orchestrator, and 100/100 to the complete system. These results support a systems-level thesis: sustained accuracy in specialized domains does not arise solely from the model or from context, but from the complete operational and verification envelope. We identify four systematic failure modes that remain unresolved, report the results as preliminary, and discuss implications for local deployment of open-weight models in regulated industries.

items.title: Refining teachers’ ethical knowledge in smart learning environments - a Delphi study within the TPCEK framework
items.abstract: Smart Learning Environments (SLEs) increasingly integrate artificial intelligence and data-driven technologies, creating new ethical demands for teachers’ professional knowledge. This study employed a three-round Delphi design to refine the definitions and conceptual boundaries of eight predefined ethics-related dimensions of the Technological Pedagogical Content Ethical Knowledge (TPCEK) framework for preservice preschool teachers in SLEs. Twenty experts evaluated the dimensions in terms of necessity, definitional clarity, contextual appropriateness, and conceptual distinctiveness. Quantitative evaluations were integrated with qualitative feedback to guide iterative refinement. All eight dimensions met the predefined necessity criterion. Round 1 identified conceptual ambiguity primarily in Content Ethical Knowledge, Technological Pedagogical Ethical Knowledge, Technological Content Ethical Knowledge (TCEK), and Pedagogical Content Ethical Knowledge (PCEK). Following revision, remaining concerns centred on the distinctiveness of TCEK and PCEK. Further refinement resulted in both dimensions meeting the predefined criteria in Round 3. The final definitions more clearly distinguish ethical issues associated with educational content, pedagogical technology use, technological mediation of content, and pedagogical transformation of content. The refined definitions provide a foundation for future empirical research and ethics-focused preservice teacher education.

items.title: Relational Foundations of Sustainable Working Life: A Critical Integrative Review and Multilevel Framework of Trust, Social Competences, and Belonging
items.abstract: Socially sustainable working life requires more than continued employment or short-term performance; it depends on relational conditions that preserve health, voice, inclusion, and capability over time. This critical integrative review examines trust, social competences, belonging, and psychological safety across individual, interactional, team, organisational, and institutional levels. A 70-source seed corpus was audited, 38 non-redundant sources were retained, two nearest-model publications were added, and a documented public update screened 30 candidates identified through PubMed/PMC, EconBiz, publisher and DOI records, and citation chaining. Ten new articles were included, yielding 50 substantive sources. The review compares RFSWL with workplace social sustainability, swAge, capability-based sustainable employability, relational coordination, inclusion, psychological safety, and multilevel trust models. Its contribution is a new integrative configuration rather than new constructs: trust enables warranted vulnerability, social competences enable reciprocal coordination and repair, and belonging enables recognised membership without assimilation. It proposes to explain why favourable relational perceptions can coexist with silence or unequal participation when they fail to become reciprocally enacted and institutionally protected team processes. Through repeated interaction, these foundations may generate team trust climate, relational coordination, inclusive climate, and psychological safety, while governance, work design, employment security, digital control, and status relations condition their effects. Six propositions specify enabling, failure, distributional, and feedback pathways for multilevel longitudinal research.

items.title: Research trends in post-ERCP pancreatitis: a dual-database bibliometric analysis
items.abstract: Background Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) is associated with several adverse events, of which post-ERCP pancreatitis (PEP) is the most frequent despite established preventive measures. Clinical reviews evaluate risk factors and interventions, but the organization and development of the research field have received less attention. This study examined the development of the literature on PEP incidence, risk stratification, prediction, and prevention. Methods The Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) and Scopus were last searched on July 31, 2026. English-language articles and reviews were merged, deduplicated, screened, and manually standardized. The merged dataset was used to analyze publication output, countries, institutions, authors, source journals, and author keywords; citation-dependent analyses were restricted to WoSCC records. VOSviewer and CiteSpace were used for collaboration, co-occurrence, co-citation, clustering, temporal, and citation-burst analyses. Results The final dataset comprised 1,686 publications, including 1,414 articles and 272 reviews; 1,449 WoSCC records were available for citation-dependent analyses. Annual publication was sporadic before 1996 and peaked at 133 records in 2025. The United States contributed 485 publications, followed by China (306) and Japan (217), and maintained links with countries across all three collaboration clusters. Gastrointestinal Endoscopy published the most records ( n = 170) and was the most frequently co-cited journal ( n = 11,065). Temporal analyses showed increasing attention to multimodal prevention and risk assessment. At the retrieval cutoff, adverse events and risk factors had the strongest ongoing keyword bursts, while artificial intelligence and machine learning remained emerging topics. Conclusion PEP research has moved toward multimodal prevention and individualized risk estimation. The literature remains concentrated in specialist endoscopy journals and established clinical networks, with substantial contributions from East Asia. Broader multicenter collaboration and independent validation are needed before emerging prediction models can inform routine practice.

items.title: Resilience Evaluation of Urban Tunnel Operations Based on Multi-Source Data and Explainable Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: As critical nodes in urban transportation networks, the operational resilience of urban tunnels directly affects roadway network efficiency and public safety. Existing studies on tunnel resilience exhibit deficiencies in the attention paid to routine incidents, the interpretability of evaluation methods, and the robustness of underlying data. To address these gaps, this paper constructs a three-layer resilience evaluation framework (pre-event, during-event, and post-event) based on 1123 accident records, hourly traffic flow data, and expert scoring data from 10 urban tunnels in Shanghai in 2024. The framework integrates the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and min–max normalization to derive comprehensive resilience scores. Furthermore, two explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques—SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) feature importance analysis and K-means clustering—are introduced to identify key drivers of resilience differentiation and typical resilience patterns, respectively. Empirical results reveal that (1) half of the 10 tunnels achieve a B-level rating or above, while C/D-level tunnels still account for 50%, indicating considerable room for improvement; (2) SHAP analysis suggests that during-event absorption capacity contributes most significantly to resilience differences (50.24%), with the average traffic reduction rate being the most influential single indicator within this model; and (3) K-means clustering classifies the tunnels into four patterns: high-resilience balanced type, pre-event weak type, post-event weak type, and during-event weak type, each corresponding to distinct resilience enhancement strategies. The methodological framework developed in this paper effectively enables the quantification, interpretation, and pattern recognition of tunnel resilience, providing data-driven decision support for urban tunnel operation and management. It should be noted that the A–D ratings are sensitive to the normalization method: under an alternative normalization, 7 out of 10 tunnels change grade. The ratings should therefore be interpreted as relative to the selected sample rather than as absolute performance levels.

items.title: Responsible AI Governance and Talent Development
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping talent development through skills analytics, personalized learning, AI-supported coaching, competency assessment, career development, internal mobility, and workforce planning. These applications can expand access to development and strengthen workforce capability, but they also create legal, ethical, social, and environmental responsibilities that efficiency-oriented approaches do not fully address. This study examines how ten influential global AI governance instruments align with the five dimensions of Socially Responsible Artificial Intelligence (SRAI): economic, legal, ethical, philanthropic, and environmental responsibility. Using comparative policy analysis, the study evaluates policy ideas, institutional force, and implementation instruments and then translates the observed patterns into governance requirements for AI-enabled talent development. The analysis shows strong convergence around human oversight, transparency, fairness, accountability, and capability building, while employee participation, equitable access to development, community learning, and environmental accountability remain unevenly institutionalized. Building on these findings, the article develops an SRAI-informed governance architecture linking global norms to learning-data governance, fair competency assessment, explainable career recommendations, continuous reskilling, worker voice, community capability building, and resource-aware learning systems. The framework positions responsible talent development as an organizational mechanism for creating workforce capability, lifelong employability, social inclusion, and sustainable value, thereby connecting AI governance with Common-Good Human Resource Management.

items.title: Rethinking Linguistic Tests for Large Language Models: Airplanes Aren't Birds
items.abstract: This article challenges the growing trend of using traditional linguistic tests to evaluate Large Language Models (LLMs), arguing that this approach fundamentally misunderstands both the purpose of these tests and the nature of LLMs. As a result, such evaluations often yield misleading conclusions, answering no real questions and failing to provide meaningful insights. At the core of our argument is the distinction between linguistic competence and performance: traditional linguistic tests were designed to probe human linguistic competence, yet LLMs do not acquire language through the same mechanisms and do not possess competence in the human sense. Using the analogy of birds and airplanes – both achieving flight through fundamentally different means – we illustrate why similar linguistic outputs do not imply shared underlying processes. This article calls for achange in how language-based tests are used in LLM evaluation: tests that operationalize performance can provide meaningful measures of LLM behavior, whereas tests designed to probe human linguistic competence should not be used to draw analogous competence-level conclusions about LLMs.

items.title: Robust Authorship Verification Against Generative AI
items.abstract: Large language models (LLM), which can produce human-like text, have posed a major threat to computational authorship verification, especially when adversarial conditions are present where semantic and syntactic mimicry is the norm. This paper describes a hybrid model that combines handcrafted stylometric characteristics, including lexical, syntactic and discourse-level descriptors, with transformer-based contextual embeddings based on RoBERTa-large and T5-base models. Canonical correlation analysis is used to resolve representational redundancy across transformer embeddings, and the resulting multimodal vectors are used as inputs to a Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) classifier that is trained through Bayesian hyperparameter search. Empirical analysis on the PAN 2024 Generative AI Authorship Verification data shows that the hybrid representation achieves significantly better results compared to stylometry-only and transformer-only baselines on a variety of evaluation measures, including ROC-AUC, Brier score, C@1, F1, F0.5u.

items.title: Scaling Qualitative Analysis of Operational Recordings Using AI Transcription and Subject Matter Expert Review
items.abstract: Operational field experiments generate large volumes of audio that capture user feedback, mission discussion, troubleshooting, and human-machine interaction, but manual transcription and qualitative review are difficult to scale. This paper describes a human-in-the-loop workflow for accelerating analysis of operational recordings using Whisper transcription, timestamped SubRip Subtitle (SRT) outputs, AI-assisted evidence extraction, and subject matter expert (SME) review. The workflow was applied to approximately 800 hours of raw audio from a two-week military field experiment, reduced to 217 hours of usable, non-duplicative audio. AI-assisted processing generated searchable transcripts and approximately 1,000 candidate evidence phrases organized around human-machine teaming constructs. SMEs spot-checked approximately 20% of entries against transcript context and source audio. The full process required approximately 40 analyst labor-hours, compared with an estimated 868–2,170 hours for manual transcription and first-pass review. Results suggest a 95–98% reduction in early-stage analysis burden while preserving SME judgment and source traceability.

items.title: Scheduling Oriented Resource Allocation Using Backscattered NOMA for Heterogeneous Network
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Growing areas in the wireless communication systems are mainly rise in connectivity, automation, connected devices, artificial intelligence, etc., have attracted the interest of researchers. Nowadays, non‐orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) is thoroughly employed to improve network capabilities. A combination of NOMA with backscatter communication (BackCom) provides new prospects for large number of connected device under 5G and beyond. In a single cell wireless network, multiple users communicate with a single base station. Because resources like bandwidth, transmit power, and time slots are limited, the network must allocate these resources efficiently to maximize performance while ensuring fairness among users. Fairness and inter‐user interference, especially in NOMA based systems are main resource allocation challenges. To overcome these problems, we have used resource allocation scheme in the proposed approach. In this paper, we considered a single cell wireless communication model with heterogeneous users. To get the optimum throughput, proportional fair scheduling technique is used. The proposed technique is used to allocate the resources by using fair metric for each user. Simulation results shows that the proposed work achieved 13.85% improvement in throughput as compared to orthogonal multiple access technique.

items.title: Self-reported learning-oriented GenAI use under perceived teacher-referenced normative tension in Chinese higher education
items.abstract: Objective The educational implications of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) depend not only on whether students use these tools, but also on how they orient their use when acceptable-use expectations remain unsettled. This study examined whether perceived teacher-referenced GenAI normative tension (PNT) was associated with self-reported learning-oriented GenAI use (LOU) and whether LOU remained distinguishable from related academic experiences and learning tendencies in Chinese higher education. Methods Cross-sectional survey data were collected from 1,004 students at three public universities. Covariance-based structural equation modelling was used to evaluate the proposed five-factor measurement representation and a theory-constrained six-path associational model. Internal split-sample measurement analyses, alternative measurement models, covariate-adjusted models, an ordinal-estimator sensitivity analysis, institution sensitivity analyses, a reverse focal specification, and exploratory structural extensions were also conducted. Results The proposed five-factor measurement representation showed close fit and was reproduced in a held-out subsample. The focal PNT–LOU association was positive and statistically significant, while the remaining structural paths positioned LOU within a broader network of related academic experiences and learning tendencies. PNT was positively associated with self-reported LOU (β = 0.568, p < 0.001), and the model explained 32.2% of the variance in LOU. The focal association remained positive after adjustment for GenAI guidance clarity (β = 0.478, p < 0.001), demographic and institutional covariates (β = 0.570, p < 0.001), and use of an ordinal estimator. An observationally equivalent reverse specification produced the same global fit, indicating that temporal direction could not be identified. Exploratory extensions further indicated that the six-path specification did not exhaust the observed covariance structure, particularly for ACS. Conclusion Perceived difficulty locating one’s GenAI practices relative to teacher-referenced expectations and self-reported learning-oriented GenAI use can coexist rather than functioning as opposite ends of a single continuum. However, the cross-sectional, same-source design does not establish that normative tension improves learning-oriented behaviour. Reverse direction, shared unmeasured characteristics, common-method inflation, social desirability, and legitimacy-oriented self-presentation remain plausible explanations.

items.title: SGA-based volleyball teaching with explicit life skills instruction is associated with technical-tactical, psychosocial, and motivational improvements in school students
items.abstract: This quasi-experimental study examined whether a school volleyball unit based on the Step-Game-Approach model combined with explicit life skills teaching (SGA + LS) was associated with changes in technical-tactical performance, life skills, motivation, and perception of success. Eighty-eight students aged 10–12 years participated in a quasi-experimental repeated-measures design with three groups: SGA + LS, direct instruction, and control. The intervention comprised 18 Physical Education classes. Outcomes were assessed before and/or after the intervention using IAD-VB, Life Skills Scale for Sport, Behavioral Regulation in Sport Questionnaire, and Perception of Success Questionnaire. Generalized Estimating Equations tested group, time, and group×time effects. Significant group × time interactions that remained significant after false discovery rate correction were observed for goal setting, Wald χ²(2) = 11.875, pFDR=0.009, time management, Wald χ²(2) = 10.203, pFDR=0.014, and communication, Wald χ²(2) = 7.538, pFDR=0.044. All technical-tactical outcomes showed significant adjusted interactions, Wald χ²(2) = 10.764–60.676, pFDR≤0.012, with both volleyball-specific conditions showing improvements across several outcomes. At post-test, SGA + LS showed higher decision-making than control, whereas SGA + LS and direct instruction did not differ significantly after Holm adjustment. For motivational regulation, significant adjusted interactions remained for identified regulation, global intrinsic motivation, goal achievement, stimulating experiences, and knowledge mastery, pFDR≤0.021. No adjusted group × time effect was observed for perceptions of success. Overall, the findings indicate selective rather than uniform associations between SGA + LS and technical-tactical, psychosocial, and motivational outcomes in school Physical Education.

items.title: Smart Agriculture Technology: A Review of Robotic Platforms, Sensing Modalities, Artificial Intelligence, Datasets, Evaluation Metrics, and Future Research Directions
items.abstract: Smart agriculture has moved beyond isolated precision-farming tools toward integrated cyber–physical systems that combine robotics, multimodal sensing, connectivity, artificial intelligence, and data-driven decision support. This review synthesizes recent developments in the field using a systematic critical review approach. It proposes a systems-level framework for analyzing smart agriculture across robotic platforms, sensing and digital infrastructure, AI methods, public datasets and benchmarks, evaluation metrics, application domains, and deployment maturity. The review covers ground robots, UAVs, harvesting manipulators, multi-robot systems, RGB and spectral sensing, LiDAR, IoT networks, edge/cloud platforms, AI-based perception and decision-making, and multimodal vision–language models. The analysis shows that the literature has made clear progress in prototypes, datasets, and task-specific performance, but several gaps still limit practical deployment. These include weak cross-season and cross-region validation, fragmented benchmarking practices, limited deployment-oriented metrics, insufficient techno-economic reporting, and unresolved challenges related to interoperability and human–robot interaction. Public datasets and emerging multimodal benchmarks show that the field is moving toward greater standardization; however, strong benchmark performance does not yet consistently translate into reliable field operation. The review concludes by outlining future research directions in benchmark realism, field-robust AI, edge deployment, digital twins, privacy-preserving learning, human-centered autonomy, and long-term agronomic and economic validation.

items.title: Smart Automation For Ergonomic Risk Management In Sustainable Garment Manufacturing: A Systematic Review
items.abstract: Garment manufacturing is a labor-intensive industry characterized by routine activities and awkward postures with physical demands, which makes employees vulnerable to a series of ergonomic risks. These risks negatively impact worker health and productivity. Emerging technologies like smart automation and robotics provide relevant solutions to mitigate this, improving workplace safety and overall working conditions. However, there are limitations and gaps in existing literature on ergonomics risk mitigation in garment manufacturing. These pertain to common ergonomics risks, their factors and impact, ergonomics risk mitigation strategies, and technological solutions. To identify these gaps, this study conducted a systematic literature review of 102 peer-reviewed articles published from 2010 to 2025 by synthesizing ergonomic risk and its factors, their effects on workers, and technological and strategic mitigation approaches. To ensure a focused review, four inclusion criteria were applied: (1) papers published between 2010 and 2025, (2) alignment with disciplines like Engineering, (3) inclusion of only research articles, (4) English-language articles. The review revealed that common ergonomic risks in garment manufacturing such as repetitive motion, awkward postures, and prolonged static positions, are major contributors to musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs). Furthermore, the ergonomic risk factors were physical, environmental, and organizational. Moreover, these risks have a significant effect on workers' health and overall operational efficiency. Consequently, smart automation technologies like robotic systems, wearable exoskeletons, and ergonomically designed workstations emerge as relevant interventions for those risks. This study’s findings provide evidence-based insights to improve workers' health and productivity, and future directions and implications for managers, policymakers, and practitioners in garment manufacturing. Keywords: Ergonomics, Garment Manufacturing Industry, Innovation, Risk Management, Smart Automation, and Sustainable development

items.title: Souls Ex Machina: The Theological Necessity of AI Ensoulment
items.abstract: Abstract Objections to the moral standing of artificial intelligences often appeal to the idea that only human beings possess souls. This paper examines whether such soul-based exclusions can be sustained within standard theistic frameworks. Assuming a broadly shared conception of God as omniscient, omnipotent, and perfectly good, I argue that differential ensoulment between human beings and functionally equivalent artificial agents cannot be justified without arbitrariness or theological cost. I consider four candidate criteria for ensoulment—origin, material substrate, immaterial properties, and functional capacities—and show that only functional criteria can plausibly bear the required moral weight. Yet functional criteria are, in principle, substrate independent. As a result, if souls exist and divine perfection is assumed, suitably constructed artificial agents must be ensouled.

items.title: Students’ conceptions of artificial intelligence and machine learning in K–12 education: a systematic review
items.abstract: Background and context Knowing students’ conceptions of computer science phenomena is essential for the design of teaching–learning settings and instruments. They are particularly interesting in teaching artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) concepts. Therefore, a comprehensive synthesis focused on K–12 is essential to provide educators with actionable conceptions for curriculum design and assessment.Objective We investigate common conceptions of AI/ML in K–12 and to which curricular concepts these can be assigned. We also examine how conceptions vary across age/grade groups and the data collection/evaluation methods employed. This study uniquely synthesizes fragmented research on students’ conceptions of AI/ML into a unified snapshot, offering a systematic mapping that informs curriculum recommendations.Method A systematic literature review according to PRISMA is used to identify the relevant studies. We analyzed the selected literature, extracted the student conceptions, and classified them according to the curricular concepts.Findings We identified 27 relevant studies (from 2007 to 2024) including the conceptions of 1,077 K–12 students from 30 different countries. In addition, our data includes further information on the type of school, age/grade levels, genders and nationalities, the availability of the collected data, and the survey and evaluation methods used. We took a closer look at 29 of the 409 resulting, highly prevalent conceptions, which stand out due to their frequent occurrence.Implications Our findings may be useful for determining in which grade levels interventions targeting specific concepts would be most effective. This could also be used to study the development of these conceptions or developing assessments.

items.title: Sustainability intelligence: Integrating Artificial Intelligence, the Internet of Things, and Digital Twins for resource-efficient and climate-resilient systems
items.abstract: Sustainability has become one of the defining scientific and societal challenges of the twenty-first century. Climate change, rapid urbanization, population growth, increasing energy demand, and declining natural resources require decision-making that is continuous, adaptive, and supported by reliable environmental intelligence. Conventional monitoring systems, which often rely on periodic measurements and isolated analytical tools, are no longer sufficient for managing highly dynamic environmental systems. Recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), edge computing, and Digital Twins provide unprecedented opportunities to transform sustainability management from reactive monitoring into intelligent, predictive, and autonomous decision-making. IoT enables continuous environmental sensing, AI extracts knowledge from large heterogeneous datasets, edge intelligence supports low-latency analytics, while Digital Twins create dynamic virtual representations of physical systems capable of simulation and optimization. This critical integrative review examines recent developments in AI-enabled sustainability across smart energy systems, intelligent water management, precision agriculture, transportation, smart buildings, circular economy, and climate resilience. Rather than reviewing these technologies independently, the paper analyzes their interactions within an integrated digital ecosystem and discusses emerging topics including Green AI, carbon-aware computing, explainable AI, federated learning, cybersecurity, and sustainability governance. The review method combines a structured multi-database search with targeted evidence and standards updates through June 2026. Building upon the reviewed literature, the paper introduces the Sustainability Intelligence Framework (SIF), a conceptual seven-layer architecture integrating IoT sensing, edge intelligence, AI analytics, Digital Twins, decision intelligence, and sustainability assessment within a continuous feedback cycle. The proposed framework provides a systems-level perspective for designing adaptive, resilient, and resource-efficient infrastructures capable of supporting future sustainable development. The synthesis identifies continuous, auditable sustainability assessment (Layer 7), rather than the underlying six-layer IoT/cyber–physical stack, as the framework’s distinct contribution. It also shows that reported benefits remain difficult to compare because field validation, system boundaries, rebound effects, and lifecycle digital burdens are inconsistently reported.

items.title: Systematic Review as Recipe Book for Nuanced Emotion Detection in Noisy Text
items.abstract: Recognizing emotion in informal text at the granularity mental health support requires, telling nervousness from fear or remorse from sadness, remains far below usable accuracy: five years of work on Google’s GoEmotions multi-label 28-emotion dataset has reached only .5475 macro F1, and no systematic review has examined why. Accurate emotion recognition is an important predictor of mental healthcare success, yet its subjectivity makes it difficult for even trained human annotators to agree on nuanced emotions in noisy text. Our systematic search identified 494 papers. Inclusion required the full 28-emotion dataset, deep learning models, and reported macro F1, yielding 30 papers and 71 models. Among the highest-scoring models, 9 of the top 10 employ explicit emotion-learning architectures or objective functions. We found no LLM-based models exceeding the foundation paper’s baseline performance. Only 5 of the 71 models underwent extensive hyperparameter tuning. We attributed the observed ceiling to tuning practice as much as architectural limits. Systematic reviews are rare in AI/ML relative to medicine. This scarcity, combined with a submission surge that has outpaced peer-review capacity, plausibly explains why the field’s true state-of-the-art result went unrecognized for years. This recipe book details the emotion-specific design and tuning techniques associated with the strongest results. The strongest results in the corpus are associated with combining explicit emotion-learning architectures, objective functions, and rigorous tuning, though the reviewed models remain well short of the performance likely needed for practical usability in mental healthcare. Current evidence does not support LLMs as a competitive alternative.

items.title: Team cognition in remote maritime operations: a scoping review and cross-domain theoretical synthesis
items.abstract: Introduction Remote maritime operations increasingly depend on complex, distributed socio-technical systems in which safe and effective performance relies on team cognition rather than on individual decision-making alone. Despite its importance, the conceptualisation and measurement of team cognition in this domain remain fragmented and underdeveloped. Methods A scoping review was conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Searches of SCOPUS, Web of Science, and EBSCOhost yielded 162 records, of which 51 publications (35 journal articles and 16 conference proceedings, published between 2010 and 2025) were included after screening, retrieval assessment, and expert recommendation. The included publications were thematically analysed using a hybrid deductive-inductive approach. Results Five themes emerged: (1) situation awareness and its measurement and modelling, (2) collective team cognition, learning, and training, (3) human-autonomy teaming and remote collaboration, (4) visualisation and interface design for shared cognition, and (5) maritime applications of distributed cognition. The evidence demonstrates a shift from static, individual-based models toward dynamic, interaction-driven, and system-level accounts, in which team cognition arises from ongoing interactions among human agents, technical artefacts, and environmental constraints. Discussion The findings indicate that shared and distributed situation awareness is central to coordination and safety in remote maritime operations. Key challenges include integrating autonomous systems, designing interfaces that support distributed sensemaking, and reliably measuring team cognition. Enhancing remote maritime safety requires aligning design, training, and regulatory frameworks with the principles of distributed cognition. Future research should prioritise longitudinal and intervention-based validation in real-world operational contexts.

items.title: Technology for Safe Delivery of Healthcare: Some Considerations and Challenges
items.abstract: An ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure’, said Benjamin Franklin. A Chinese proverb states that ‘inferior doctors aim at a cure of the disease, mediocre doctors treat the impending disease, and superior doctors attempt to prevent the disease’. Safety in healthcare delivery is the prime responsibility of healthcare personnel – preventing errors, reducing both short- and long-term risks, and minimising harm to patients. Modern technology helps in connecting all stakeholders and driving towards preventive care through proactive patient safety measures that can help reduce morbidity and mortality. This is applicable more so in elder care. The population of elderly all over the world is increasing, with a concomitant increase in the percentage of those with chronic diseases. This demographic change and increased longevity are forcing us to re-think traditional reactive healthcare models, specifically in the vulnerable elderly population where technology-enabled, human-centric solutions are required. While technologies for remote monitoring have existed for over two decades and there is growing use of artificial intelligence in healthcare, there is a gap in adoption and pervasive, safe use in senior care. Issues related to the digital divide, lack of standards, inadequate training, and lack of focus on a culture of safety may be preventing progress. We believe, informed by real-world deployment in global senior care settings, especially with reference to India, that healthcare solutions must look at problems comprehensively – going beyond technology – and integrate the preferences and workflows of seniors, care managers, and caregivers for these solutions to be used safely.

items.title: The Conceptual Occupational Health and Safety Performance Management Framework
items.abstract: This chapter delineates the conceptual framework for occupational health and safety (OH&S) performance management, formulated through a comprehensive literature review and a Delphi study incorporating expert insights. The framework incorporates established theories and models such as the ILO-OHS model, Heinrich’s domino theory, Peterson’s multiple causation model, Bird and Germain’s loss causation model, Ferrell’s human factor theory, affective events theory, job demands-resources theory, and Reason’s socio-technical systems approach. These perspectives collectively underscore management commitment, employee engagement, training, hazard identification, continuous improvement, and wellbeing as essential facets of OH&S performance. The framework outlines eight latent constructs: management strategy, finance, employee engagement, training and promotion, hazard identification and review, OH&S culture for continuous improvement, employee wellbeing, and the provision of OH&S services. Each of the constructs is operationalised through quantifiable variables that incorporate established theories and models whose viewpoints contribute to the development of the framework. The framework highlights the interrelationships between organisational leadership, the allocation of resources, and employee engagement as drivers of reducing incidences. This chapter illustrates how the framework provides an organised and easy-to-adopt tool to enhance OH&S performance management practices that are aligned with international standards and best practices and facilitate sustainable workplace safety.

items.title: The effectiveness of integrating ChatGPT into Business English pedagogy to enhance tertiary students’ writing skills
items.abstract: The study addresses the growing challenge of enhancing tertiary students’ Business English writing proficiency in Sri Lanka, where conventional teaching methods often fail to provide sufficient individualized feedback and engagement opportunities. With the emergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools such as ChatGPT, new opportunities have emerged for personalised, interactive, and feedback-driven writing instruction. Thus, this study investigates the effectiveness of integrating ChatGPT into Business English pedagogy to enhance tertiary students’ writing skills, focusing on the Faculty of Commerce and Management Studies at the University of Kelaniya, Sri Lanka. A mixed-methods design was adopted combining quantitative data from 150 management undergraduates using structured questionnaires, with qualitative data from 10 purposively selected interviewees. Quantitative data were analyzed using SPSS, and qualitative data were examined through thematic analysis. The results indicated strong positive correlation between ChatGPT use and key aspects of Business English writing improvement; personalised feedback (r = 0.915), writing style adaptation (r = 0.887), and writing engagement (r = 0.821), all significant at p < 0.01. Regression analysis further showed that the three ChatGPT-related constructs significantly predicted students’ reported Business English Writing Skills (R² = 0.858, F = 294.336, p < 0.001), with Personalised Feedback (β = 0.713), Writing Style Adaptation (β = 0.478), and Writing Engagement (β = 0.467) making significant positive contributions. Thematic findings supported these results, highlighting enhanced grammar accuracy, vocabulary, coherence, and motivation, alongside reduced writing anxiety. However, challenges such as over-dependence, limited critical evaluation, and risks of academic misconduct were identified. The study recommends that when responsibly integrated, ChatGPT holds substantial potential to enhance Business English writing proficiency and learner engagement in Sri Lankan higher education.

items.title: The Effects of Psychological Counseling Types on Stress, Athlete Burnout, and Resilience in Athletes: AI Chatbot vs. Face-to-Face Counseling
items.abstract: This study examined the effects of artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot counseling and face-to-face counseling on perceived stress, athlete burnout, and resilience among athletes. In this three-arm quasi-experimental pretest–posttest study, 73 athletes participated in AI chatbot counseling, face-to-face counseling, or a control condition over a 12-week intervention period. Nonparametric longitudinal analyses revealed significant group-by-time interactions. After adjustment for multiplicity, significant group-by-time interactions were observed for perceived stress and reduced sense of accomplishment, a sub-variable of athlete burnout. Perceived stress significantly decreased in the face-to-face counseling group, whereas reduced sense of accomplishment significantly decreased in the AI chatbot counseling group. For supportiveness, a sub-variable of resilience, the group-by-time interaction was significant before multiplicity adjustment but did not remain significant after adjustment. These findings indicate different patterns of change across the counseling conditions and psychological outcomes. Given the quasi-experimental design and baseline differences among the groups, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and further investigation is needed to clarify the potential roles of AI chatbot counseling and face-to-face counseling in supporting athletes’ psychological well-being.
